faqih.title: Fiqh Research
faqih.intro: Ask about a matter of fiqh: the books of the library (the Kuwaiti Encyclopedia of Fiqh, al-Mughni, al-Muhalla, the primers of the schools and more) are searched, and what they say is shown word for word, with the volume, the page and a link to the place in the book.
faqih.disclaimer: This is a search of the books, not a fatwa: it shows what the scholars wrote, does not choose between their views and does not answer personal cases. For a ruling on your own case, ask a scholar.
faqih.arabicOnly: Write the question in Arabic (3 to 300 characters); the answer and the texts are in Arabic.
faqih.notFound: This matter was not found in the available books. Try other words, as the jurists put it, or ask a scholar.
faqih.referScholar: This concerns your own case and needs a ruling from a scholar who hears its details; the search does not answer it.
faqih.tooMany: Too many questions in a short time; wait a minute and try again.
faqih.busy: The search has reached its daily limit of questions; please come back tomorrow.
faqih.notReady: The search is not available right now.
kutub.title: Creed and Fiqh
kutub.intro: The primers of knowledge and its great books: the creed of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jamaʿah, hadith, fiqh in the schools, and the books of imams such as Ibn Qudamah, Ibn Hazm, Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim. Each book is complete, as printed.
kutub.aqidaIntro: The creed of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jamaʿah as its imams wrote it, with its proofs from the Quran and Sunnah.
kutub.fiqhIntro: The relied-upon primer of each of the four schools, the first book a student of fiqh studies in their school, then the great books of fiqh such as al-Mughni and al-Muhalla.
kutub.arabicOnly: The books are in Arabic, as printed.

hijri.title: Hijri calendar
hijri.adjustHint: If your country announced the new month a day before or after the Umm al-Qura calendar, adjust the date here. The adjustment applies to the prayer times too.
hijri.source: The dates follow the Umm al-Qura calendar; the actual start of each month is set by the moon sighting in your country.
hijri.noDay30: {month} has no 30th day this year: the month is 29 days long in the Umm al-Qura calendar.
hijri.sacredNote: The four sacred months are Dhul-Qaʿdah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab: sins in them weigh heavier and good deeds count for more.
hijri.monThuNote: The Prophet ﷺ sought to fast on Mondays and Thursdays, the days on which deeds are presented.
hijri.fridayNote: The best day on which the sun rises: Surat al-Kahf, prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ and supplication in its hour of acceptance.
hijri.ev.newYearNote: A new Hijri year begins. Muharram is a sacred month, and after Ramadan the best fasting is in Muharram (Muslim).
hijri.ev.tasuaNote: It is recommended to fast the 9th of Muharram together with ʿAshura.
hijri.ev.ashuraNote: Fasting the day of ʿAshura expiates the past year (Muslim).
hijri.ev.whiteNote: Fasting three days of every month is recommended, best on the 13th, 14th and 15th.
hijri.ev.ramadanNote: The month of fasting, night prayer and the Quran, in which the gates of Paradise are opened and the gates of Hell closed.
hijri.ev.lastTenNote: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in them, especially the odd nights (Bukhari); the Prophet ﷺ used to spend them in iʿtikaf.
hijri.ev.fitrNote: Fasting on the day of Eid is forbidden. Zakat al-fitr is given before the Eid prayer, and the takbir is said from the night of Eid until the prayer.
hijri.ev.sixShawwalNote: Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted the whole year (Muslim).
hijri.ev.tenDhulHijjahNote: No days are dearer to Allah for good deeds than these ten days (Bukhari): fasting, dhikr and takbir.
hijri.ev.tarwiyaNote: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, when the pilgrims go out to Mina.
hijri.ev.arafahNote: Fasting it, for those not on Hajj, expiates two years (Muslim); the best supplication is that of the Day of ʿArafah.
hijri.ev.adhaNote: The day of sacrifice; fasting on it is forbidden. The Eid prayer, the sacrifice and the takbir.
hijri.ev.tashriqNote: Days of eating, drinking and remembering Allah (Muslim); no fasting on them, and the takbir continues until their end.

qibla.turnTo: Turn your phone until the arrow lines up with the Kaaba

qibla.compassDenied: Compass access was not allowed. Allow the site to use “Motion & Orientation” in the browser settings, then try again.
qibla.insecure: The compass works only over a secure connection (https). Open the app at its published address or from the installed app, or use the sun as below.
qibla.calibrate: If the compass seems off, move the phone through the air in a figure of eight a few times, away from metal and magnets.
qibla.sunHint: Without a compass: at these times today the sun stands exactly in the direction of the Qibla, or the shadow of an upright pole points to it.
qibla.sunFacing: The sun is in the direction of the Qibla
qibla.sunNone: Today the sun does not pass the direction of the Qibla or its opposite at your place.
qibla.overKaabaNote: Twice a year the sun stands exactly over the Kaaba, so at that moment its direction is the Qibla from anywhere it can be seen: {dates}.
qibla.source: The direction is calculated on your device along the great circle to the Kaaba. A phone compass is approximate and may be off by a few degrees; when you can, check against the sun or the mihrab of a nearby mosque.
prayer.source: The times are calculated astronomically on your device. If they differ from your mosque's timetable, adjust them in minutes.

about.title: About
about.hisnTitle: Hisn al-Muslim: remembrances from the Quran and Sunnah
about.hisnAuthor: By Shaykh Saʿid ibn ʿAli ibn Wahf al-Qahtani, may Allah have mercy on him.
about.hisnSource: The texts come from the book’s official website {link}: {chapters} and {adhkar}.
about.offline: The app works offline after the first visit and collects no data.
about.mushafText: The Quran text and fonts in eight readings come from the {source} and are shown exactly as published.
about.mushafOffline: Each reading is saved on the device after you first open it, so you can read it offline.
about.trText: Quran translations come from the Noble Quran Encyclopedia {link} and are shown unchanged with the translator and version. The English adhkar translation comes from the official Hisn al-Muslim website.
about.machineNote: The interface and chapter titles in this language were translated with computer assistance and need review. Adhkar and Quran texts are never machine-translated.
about.audioText: Recitations and reciter radios come from {link}, and live stations from their official sources. An internet connection is needed.
about.tafsirText: Al-Muyassar and al-Mukhtasar come from {qe}; the tafsirs of as-Saʿdi, al-Baghawi, Ibn Kathir, al-Qurtubi and at-Tabari come from the open {qul} library. They are shown as published.
about.tajweedText: A summary of the rules of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim by way of al-Shāṭibiyyah, with examples and colours from the pages of the colour-coded Tajweed Mushaf, and the verses of «Tuḥfat al-Aṭfāl» and «al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah» edited by Dr ʿAbd al-Muḥsin al-Qāsim, from {link}.
about.asmaText: The complete book “Explanation of the Beautiful Names of Allah in the light of the Quran and Sunnah” by al-Qahtani, as printed, from the {link} copy.
about.kutubText: Books of creed, hadith, fiqh and its principles, the Prophet's life and the spiritual path, complete and as printed, from the {link} copies that follow the printed editions; each book names its editor and publisher.
about.hijriText: Follows the Umm al-Qura calendar as the browser computes it, adjustable by a day or two to match the moon sighting in your country; the seasons of worship shown are those established in the Sunnah.
about.qiblaText: Calculated on your device from the place of the prayer times, along the great circle to the Kaaba; the phone's compass is read on the device and its readings never leave it. With the compass come the times at which the sun shows the Qibla.
about.prayerText: Calculated on the device with the methods of each country's authorities. City search by {geo}; place names from {osm}; alerts while the app is closed are sent by the app's server on {cf}.
about.adhanText: Adhan recordings from Wikimedia Commons under free licences, and from the Internet Archive (archive.org) and IslamWeb (islamweb.net) for the voices of the sheikhs and of the Two Holy Mosques, whose rights belong to their holders and which are removed at their request. Each was cut to the adhan alone and re-encoded:
